He spends his mornings fastidiously dusting the carvings (and literally only dusting the carvings - they're completely clean, but the hall itself is ankle-deep in dust), then spends the rest of the day sleeping or watching out the window. Out his window, he can see much of what goes on in the castle, but he's so removed from it all that he doesn't actually know for a fact exactly what's happening at any given time. So he has this detached, observational attitude toward the castle. He can work out at least some decent guesses about what's going on below him, but he doesn't in fact know, and he's comfortable with that.
